activity_context.topic_title: Writing Geometric Series in Sigma Notation

feedback.problem: The first term of a geometric sequence is $6$ and the common ratio is $-4.$ Written in sigma notation, what is the sum of the first $32$ terms?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we must express the series in the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=6,$ $r=-4$ and $N=32.$

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
{S}_{32}={\sum }_{n=1}^{32}6{(-4)}^{n-1}\,\,
$$

Finally, we can simplify the above using the laws of exponents, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{32}6{(-4)}^{n-1} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{32}6{(-4)}^{n}{(-4)}^{-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{32}6{(-4)}^{n}(-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{32}(-\frac{3}{2}){(-4)}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$
